content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Deviation — Section 22.1 (Audit Rights).**

- **Problem:** 22.1 lets Vendor audit "at any time without notice" with remote access to our systems — this is walk-away territory under the AUDIT rule and fails the fallback on frequency, notice and system access.
- **Mitigating context:** 22.2 and 22.3 are already favourable (Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access, findings are our Confidential Information, final report provided). The cost term already sits at the preferred position, so no edit was needed there — but 22.2's no-direct-access language also directly conflicts with 22.1.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** 22.1 now permits one audit per twelve-month period, on 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours without unreasonable disruption, by an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality, with no remote or direct system access (we supply usage records instead).
